# Text Repriser Collection

> Six standalone, client-side web pages that rewrite modern English into
> literary and historical styles. No backend, no build step for visitors, no
> dependencies. The live site is static and served by GitHub Pages.

Live site: https://cuber7649.github.io/shakespeare-repriser/

## Pages

- index.html — dashboard: one input, all six styles at once
- shakespeare.html — Elizabethan English
- pirate.html — Golden Age of Piracy
- victorian.html — Victorian English
- chaucer.html — Middle English
- yoda.html — Jedi Master speech (conservative word-order inversions)
- norse.html — Vikings and Norse myth

## Using it from a browser-driving agent

Every page exposes `window.Repriser` in the page context. It drives the same
input, settings and Transform button a person uses, so there is no second
engine to drift from the visible app.

```js
Repriser.styles();
// [{ id: 'shakespeare', label: 'Shakespeare' }, ... six entries]

Repriser.transformStyle('shakespeare', 'how are you', 2);
// "How dost thou fare" (possibly with a random aside; see Seed below)

Repriser.transformAll('how are you', 2);
// { shakespeare: '...', pirate: '...', ... } on index.html

Repriser.transform('how are you', 2, { intensity: 'light', asides: false });
// object keyed by style id: one key on a style page, six on the dashboard
```

Signatures:

- `styles()` — array of `{ id, label }`.
- `transform(text, seed?, options?)` — object keyed by style id.
- `transformStyle(id, text, seed?, options?)` — one string. On a style page the
  id must match that page; the dashboard accepts any of the six.
- `transformAll(text, seed?, options?)` — object with every available output.

`seed` defaults to 1 for reproducibility; pass the same input, seed and options
to get the same output. Omit the seed only when you want the page's natural
variation. `options` accepts `intensity` (`light`, `balanced`, `dramatic`) and
the booleans `openings`, `metaphors`, `asides`, `invert`; `false` disables one.
Calling these methods changes the visible input, settings and results.

## Quote card: making an image from the output

Each page can turn the current result into a shareable 1080x1350 PNG. There is
no separate image-generation endpoint; the card is drawn in the browser from
the text already in the output. Authored asides and stage directions are
dropped, but bracketed text written in the input is kept.

1. Produce the text with `Repriser.transform(...)` or by clicking Transform.
2. Open the card modal by clicking `[data-agent-action="card"]`. On index.html
   there is one per style, so use `#cardBtn-<style>` to pick one.
3. The preview is `#cardPreview`. Optional settings live in the modal:
   `#cardSkin` (`auto`, `parchment`, `midnight`, `verdant`), `#cardBackground`
   (`gradient`, `flat`, `wash`), `#cardAlign` (`left`, `center`, `right`), and
   the `#cardOriginal` checkbox to add the original text in a band below.
4. Click `#cardDownload` to save the PNG, or `#cardClose` to dismiss. A long
   quote sets `#cardModalWarn` visible; `#cardStatus` announces the result.

## Stable browser hooks

All seven pages use the same `data-agent-action` attributes, so an agent does
not need to guess per-style button text:

- `[data-agent-action="transform"]`, `"surprise"`, `"clear"` — one each.
- `[data-agent-action="copy"]`, `"save"`, `"compare"`, `"card"` — one per
  output on a style page, six on the dashboard.
- `.surprise-sample[data-sample="layoff|breakup|grocery"]` — quick-sample chips
  that fill a ready-made scenario and transform it in one click.

Inputs and outputs: `#input`, `#charCount`, `#output` (style pages) or
`#out-<style>` (dashboard). Status messages use `role="status"` regions.
